questions.prompt: Which of these countries covers the most ground?

hints.nudge: Area is how much ground a country covers, not how many people live there. A small crowded country can still be small.
hints.whereToLook: Compare the four on the Atlas. Area means how much ground a country covers.

questions.proof: By area: Bolivia about 1,098,581 square kilometres; Nicaragua about 120,340 square kilometres; Solomon Islands about 28,400 square kilometres; Mauritius about 2,040 square kilometres.

questions.prompt: True or false: “Bolivia shares a land border with Monaco.”

hints.nudge: Read the statement slowly. Does it match what the article says, or has one word been swapped for another?
hints.whereToLook: Look at the Atlas and see which countries touch it.

questions.proof: Bolivia borders Argentina, Brazil, Chile, Paraguay, Peru.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Bolivia?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Bolivia article.

questions.proof: The main languages are Spanish and Quechua, but there are other languages too.

questions.prompt: What money is used in Bolivia?

hints.nudge: Money names often come from a country’s own words. The other three are spent in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the part of the article about the economy, or at the facts for the country.

questions.proof: The money used in Bolivia is the boliviano.

hints.nudge: A continent is one of the great land masses of the world. Find Bolivia on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
hints.whereToLook: Find Bolivia on the Atlas and see which land mass it sits on.
